scope: Proposition 6.3 (The tower properties) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-the-Kadison-Kaplansky-Projection-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df6227b615985805), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all sufficiently large ℓ, the preceding choices give a graph Y 0 on sets of sizes |Ai| = d2Hi and |Bi| = 2Hi , and its induced subgraph Y , with these properties. 1. For every |i − k| ≤ 1, the Y 0-block between Ai and Bk has degrees d, Dik with Dik = D2|i|−|k|. Its counting incidence divided by √ dDik maps normalized constants to normalized constants, as does its adjoint. On their orthogonal complements its norm is at most 1 − χ, with the absolute constant χ of Proposition 5.4. 2. The fraction removed from any Ai or Bi is at most εℓ of (6.5). 3. The labels of Y are folded, with positive alphabet size at most mℓ = O(d2r(1 + s)2). 4. Every nonbacktracking path in Y beginning at layer i and having length at least Li is deter- mined by its oriented word among all paths in Y , including paths beginning in other layers. 5. There is no nonempty cyclically nonbacktracking closed path in Y , based at layer i, of length at most gi.
